annotation.title_clean: Clearview AI Inc v The Information Commissioner
annotation.title_en: Clearview AI Inc v The Information Commissioner
annotation.authors_or_issuer: First-tier Tribunal (General Regulatory Chamber, Information Rights), United Kingdom
annotation.venue: Find Case Law - The National Archives
annotation.summary_en: UK First-tier Tribunal decision allowing Clearview AI's appeal against the ICO's enforcement and monetary penalty notices. The tribunal found the processing related to behavioural monitoring under Article 3(2)(b) UK GDPR, but fell outside the GDPR's material scope because clients were foreign law enforcement and national security agencies, so the ICO lacked jurisdiction.
key_provisions_or_claims: Appeal allowed: the ICO lacked jurisdiction to issue the Enforcement Notice and Monetary Penalty Notice.
Article 3(2)(b) can apply where a third party (the client) carries out the monitoring, not only the controller.
Clearview's processing related to monitoring of UK data subjects' behaviour by its clients.
Processing for foreign state law enforcement and national security is outside material scope under Article 2(2)(a) GDPR and Article 3(2A) UK GDPR.
The tribunal did not decide whether Clearview actually breached GDPR provisions.
